BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**For:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Seller's covering note, "Key Negotiated Positions" summary and Disclosure Letter. I have not seen the full SPA clause text, so drafting points should be checked against the actual mark-up.

## Preliminary points on how to read these documents

1. **"Negotiated positions" does not mean agreed.** The Seller labels its summary "Key Negotiated Positions" and describes the funds flow as reflecting the "agreed price mechanics." Neither is agreed on our side. Treat every item as a Seller proposal.
2. **Matching a fallback number does not clear a point.** The Seller's 20% / AUD 4.8m cap and 18-month claims period match our internal fallbacks exactly. Amelia Frost has given no written authority for either fallback for this draft. We should not concede them, and we should not tell the Seller they are within our range. The Seller should not know our fallbacks, so the match itself is worth noting to the deal team.
3. **The disclosure facts are stale.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026, about six weeks ago. Before relying on any item, we need a refreshed position from the Seller on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006 and the bonuses. We should also separate facts we have verified from Seller assertions.
4. **Clause 1.4 is a non-admission clause.** The Seller does not admit that any consent, payment, notice or remediation is required. That is acceptable as a disclosure caveat. It must not later be used to argue that a Condition or Completion deliverable is unnecessary.

## Issue-by-issue analysis

### A. Liability regime

| # | Seller position | Playbook | Assessment / pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | **Cap 20% / AUD 4.8m** (cl 12.1) | 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% only with Amelia Frost's written authority, which has not been given. | **Reject; restate 25% / AUD 6.0m.** Make no concession without written authority identifying this draft. |
| A2 | **De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000, excess only** (cl 12.2) | De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000, recovery from the first dollar | **Reject.** The de minimis is 5× ours and the basket is 5× ours. The "excess only" (deductible) mechanism means we would absorb AUD 250k of proven loss permanently. Restate AUD 5k / AUD 50k on a tipping basis. |
| A3 | **18-month general claims period** (cl 12.3/13) | 24 months. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's approval, which has not been given. | **Reject; restate 24 months.** |
| A4 | **"Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"** | Keep categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | **Reject.** This is a sweep-up that silently imports the general cap, basket and time limits into Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnity, payment and covenant claims. Reverse the default: general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims. |
| A5 | **Title and capacity under the general caps and time limits** "for administrative simplicity" | Separate fundamental regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | **Reject firmly.** "Administrative simplicity" is no justification. Title is the core of what we are buying. On the Seller's draft, a defect in title to the shares would be capped at AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m deal and barred after 18 months. |
| A6 | **Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"** (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of everything, to the maximum extent enforceable. Not waivable. | **Reject; non-negotiable.** As drafted this extends to fraud and wilful concealment. Insert an express carve-out from caps, baskets, de minimis, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. No one on the team has authority to waive this. |

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

| # | Seller position | Assessment / pushback |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | **General disclosure of the entire data room and DD-002 to DD-012** (DL 1.1) | **Reject.** Require specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties, with enough detail for us to assess nature and scope. A whole-data-room disclosure moves all diligence risk to us. |
| B2 | **Deemed disclosure of Accounts, statutory registers and public records** (DL 1.2) | **Reject.** At most, allow specific items identified in the letter. No deemed disclosure from public registers or searches. |
| B3 | **Blanket buyer-knowledge bar covering advisers and anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records** (cl 8.3) | **Delete.** It is wider than actual knowledge and would effectively give the Seller a second general disclosure. If any qualifier survives, it must be limited to the actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals. Any Seller-side awareness qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. No knowledge qualifier may ever excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. |

### C. Conditions and Completion deliverables

**C1. Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3). Material.**
- Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of FY26 revenue (DD-002), and its contract has a change-control consent (cl 11.2) with conditions (cl 11.3).
- The Seller offers only **reasonable endeavours** and treats the consent as satisfied **on delivery of a written consent**. That is consent-on-delivery and could be met by a consent whose cl 11.3 conditions remain unsatisfied.
- The Disclosure Letter confirms that at 22 Sept no final consent or evidence of condition satisfaction existed.
- **Push back:** make it a Condition Precedent that requires (a) an effective, unconditional written consent from Bluefen (or one whose conditions are all satisfied) and (b) evidence satisfactory to the Buyer that the cl 11.3 conditions are met, both before Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient. Ask for a current status update.

**C2. Riverlark facility (cl 2/7). Material.**
- About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with change-control (cl 8.1) and discharge (cl 9.2) provisions. The Seller offers a release "to be provided following Completion."
- This is inconsistent with debt-free/cash-free: we would be paying for a company still encumbered at Completion.
- **Push back:** require a current payout letter, repayment directly from Completion funds as a funds-flow line, and executed security releases (including PPSR discharges) delivered at Completion. A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval, neither of which we have. Confirm the AUD 3.2m figure against a current payout statement, since the "approximately" figure is six weeks old.

**C3. Employee bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000). Material.**
- The Seller says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. The Disclosure Letter confirms they are absent from it and says nothing on payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs.
- The bonuses are triggered by Completion. If the Company pays them after Completion, the cost falls on us. "A matter for the Seller" has no mechanism behind it.
- **Push back:** either (a) a specific funds-flow line deducted from the price (treated as Debt or a transaction liability) covering AUD 420k **plus** all triggered on-costs (PAYG withholding, payroll tax, superannuation and workers' compensation as applicable), or (b) Seller-funded payment at Completion, backed by a specific indemnity. Do not accept a funds flow that silently excludes them.

### D. Specific risk items

**D1. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1).**
- The Seller says the indemnity, limited to the SOW3 payment, is "adequate." Under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, but this is not bank-verified either way. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- The risk is ownership of the IP, not just the payment. If SOW3 is not fully paid, the Company may not own materials it uses.
- **Push back:** broaden the indemnity to cover loss from any failure of the Company to own or have full rights in the SOW3 Project Materials, including third-party claims. Preserve the cure: require payment of any outstanding SOW3 fees (from the Seller or via funds flow) plus a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay as a Completion deliverable. Do not assume AUD 180k is right; verify the amount.

**D2. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6).**
- The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." The Disclosure Letter confirms that whether anyone accessed the file, the exact scope and any notification obligation (including under the NDB scheme) are not yet established.
- We should **not** treat it as a confirmed breach, assert harm, assume notification is required or put a number on it. We also should not accept the Seller's "not material" characterisation.
- **Push back:** add pre-Completion covenants requiring preservation of logs and evidence, a proper investigation (including recall or expiry of the link and access-log review), regular written updates to the Buyer, and Buyer consultation before any regulator or individual notification. Consider a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident, kept outside the general regime. Ask for a current update, since the facts are six weeks old.

**D3. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k: 3 × AUD 110k, DD-008/DD-011).**
- The Seller asserts these are "ordinary-course operating costs." The Disclosure Letter itself says it does not state whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course, and asks that they be read together for timing and scope.
- **Our position:** assess this, without making assumptions either way. Request the contracts, renewal and termination terms, and the accounting treatment. Do not automatically classify the amounts as Debt or seek a price deduction yet. Do not accept the ordinary-course label either. Consider whether a three-way split of AUD 110k each is relevant to any approval or authority thresholds.

**D4. Tax and IP warranties.**
- The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." They are **not settled**; both remain open.
- **Push back:** reject the general-regime treatment. Keep them as separate categories with their own caps and periods, to be negotiated. Do not assume unlimited liability as our ask, and do not assume any resolution.

**D5. Title (DD-012).**
- The Seller relies on its own share register. The Disclosure Letter itself says the register is the source relied on and that we have not verified it.
- **Push back:** require independent evidence. This means an ASIC company extract cross-checked against the register, PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company, the constitution, a chain of issue and transfer documents, confirmation of no options, convertibles or other share rights, board and shareholder approvals for the sale, and a Seller capacity and authority certificate. Title warranties sit in the fundamental regime (see A5).

**D6. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).**
- The Disclosure Letter says the lease requires only notification and that Mossvale consent is not triggered by a share sale. These are the Seller's readings.
- **Action:** our counsel should confirm both from the underlying documents, checking for change-of-control definitions and indirect-assignment wording. The lease notification should become a Completion or post-Completion deliverable.

## Summary of recommendations

**Reject outright and restate the playbook:**
1. Cap of 25% / AUD 6.0m, not 20%. **No authority exists for the fallback.**
2. De minimis AUD 5k, basket AUD 50k, recovery from the first dollar.
3. General claims period of 24 months, not 18. **No authority exists for the fallback.**
4. Delete the "limitations apply to all Claims" default and keep Title, Tax, IP, indemnity, payment and covenant claims separate.
5. Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
6. **Express fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out** from all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. Non-negotiable and not waivable.
7. Specific fair disclosure only. Delete data-room, public-register and Accounts deemed disclosure.
8. Delete the cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge bar.

**Require as Conditions or Completion deliverables:**
9. Bluefen: effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a CP. Not reasonable endeavours or consent-on-delivery.
10. Riverlark: payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and security releases at Completion.
11. Bonuses: AUD 420k plus on-costs itemised in the funds flow or Seller-funded, with an indemnity.
12. Ironquay: broadened IP indemnity, payment of SOW3 and a confirmatory assignment, with the AUD 180k verified.
13. Title: independent ASIC, PPSR and corporate evidence, not just DD-012.

**Investigate before taking a position:**
14. DD-006: investigation and update covenants. No assumptions about breach, harm or notification.
15. Sandbar: obtain the contracts and assess. No automatic Debt treatment.
16. Lease and Mossvale: confirm the Seller's readings independently.

**Process:**
- Ask the Seller for a refreshed disclosure update. The 22 September position is stale.
- Do not signal flexibility on cap or period. If the team wants to use either fallback, it needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft.
- Treat Tax and IP as open items.

I can turn this into a mark-up cover note or an issues list in the Seller's clause order if that would help.
